::::: {.columns}

![](media/diffuse/icecube-2013-veto.svg){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-width: 501px; --media-max-height: 480px; --media-bg: #fff;" fig-alt="Original IceCube side-view diagram of its outer veto and inner fiducial volume, including the dust layer."}

### Glashow and flavour

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="56%"}
![](media/diffuse/icecube-glashow-event-2021.jpg){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 520px; --media-bg: #fff;" fig-alt="IceCube visualization of the December 2016 Glashow-resonance candidate: schematic of early muon light, the event view across the detector and photon arrival times at the two nearest sensors."}
:::
::: {.column width="41%"}
**Glashow resonance**

$$\bar\nu_e+e^-\to W^-\to\text{hadrons}$$

$$E_{\bar\nu}\simeq6.3\,\mathrm{PeV}$$

One shower, December 2016. Only antineutrinos can do this.

**Tau neutrinos**

Seven candidates: all three flavours arrive.

**Why it matters**

$pp$: $\ \bar\nu_e:\nu_e\approx1:1$

simple $p\gamma$: $\ \approx1:3.5$
:::
:::::

::: {.media-caption}
[IceCube, Nature 591, 220 (2021), Fig. 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.15051) · [Tau neutrinos: IceCube, PRL 132, 151001 (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.02516)
:::

::::::

:::::: {.panel-tabset}

### IceCube

<img class="slide-media media-height-lg" style="--media-max-height: 530px;" src="media/galactic/icecube-multiwavelength-2023.jpg" alt="IceCube's five Galactic-coordinate views: optical, gamma rays, predicted neutrino emission, analysis expectation and observed pre-trial significance.">

### Baikal-GVD above 200 TeV

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="63%"}
![](media/galactic/gvd-galactic-sky.svg){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 480px;" fig-alt="Redrawn sky map in Galactic coordinates: the eight Baikal-GVD cascades above 200 TeV as orange 90% containment circles; five of them lie in or next to the shaded band within 10 degrees of the Galactic plane."}
:::
::: {.column width="35%"}
**8 cascades above 200 TeV**

They crowd towards the Galactic plane.

![](media/galactic/gvd-galactic-test.svg){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 230px;" fig-alt="Median absolute Galactic latitude of the eight cascades compared with skies whose right ascensions are randomized: the data line lies in the low tail of the random-sky histogram."}

Baikal-GVD: $p=1.4\times10^{-2}$

With IceCube: $p=3.4\times10^{-4}$
:::
:::::

::: {.media-caption}
V. A. Allakhverdyan et al. (Baikal-GVD) with Y. Y. Kovalev, A. V. Plavin, D. V. Semikoz, S. V. Troitsky · [ApJ 982, 73 (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.05608v2) · Redrawn from Table 1; test of Fig. 1 recomputed
:::

### Gamma rays

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="63%"}
![](media/galactic/galactic-gamma-diffuse.svg){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 520px;" fig-alt="Redrawn published spectra of diffuse gamma rays from the Galactic plane between 10 TeV and 1 PeV: LHAASO-KM2A inner and outer Galaxy points from its tables, and Tibet AS-gamma points digitized from its Figure 4, shown as E to the 2.7 times the differential flux."}
:::
::: {.column width="35%"}
**The same collisions**

$$\pi^0\to\gamma\gamma,\qquad \pi^\pm\to\nu\ \ldots$$

The Galactic plane glows in gamma rays up to $\sim1\,\mathrm{PeV}$.

**Tibet AS$\gamma$, 2021:** first diffuse gamma rays above $100\,\mathrm{TeV}$.

**LHAASO, 2023:** the spectrum from $10\,\mathrm{TeV}$ to $1\,\mathrm{PeV}$.
:::
:::::

::: {.media-caption}
Redrawn: [LHAASO, PRL 131, 151001 (2023)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.05372v2), Tables S2–S3 · [Tibet AS$\gamma$, PRL 126, 141101 (2021)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.05181v2), digitized from Fig. 4 · Different sky regions and source masks
:::
